Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The Pakistani players have made their way out into the middle. Kraigg Brathwaite and Kieran Powell are the openers for West Indies. Mohammad Abbas to begin with the ball. Here we go...

Right then. This will be a nervy phase for the Windies openers, as there is not much time left, nor are there many overs. They will want to stay out there without losing a single wicket. Will they be able to do so? Stay tuned to find out...

Just what West Indies needed with the ball. They have bowled with intent, purpose, and zest to bowl Pakistan out for a decent score. Jason Holder was definitely the pick of the lot, as he finished with 3 to his name, while also being economical. Jayden Seales was slightly expensive but still got three wickets. Kemar Roach again showed his skill, ending with a wicket to his name. Overall, though, this was a combined bowling effort from the hosts.

Pakistan did not really have the best outing with the blade in this innings, but a couple of batting displays helped them post a decent total. They lost their openers early and just when it seemed like Azhar Ali and Babar Azam were going along nicely, this stand was broken too. Azam and Rizwan did not hang around for long too. Fawad Alam and Faheem Ashraf stitched an 85-run, which was looking solid, but once this was broken, Pakistan just kept losing wickets and folded for 217.

A really good bowling display by the hosts has seen them bundle out Pakistan for 217. The visitors will not be too unhappy about how things have panned out, as they got a couple of runs towards the end of the innings, but they would have wanted to cross the 250-run mark.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Two-in-two for Holder! That's the end of the Pakistani inning as they end on 217. A good length ball, shaping away, around off. Abbas hangs his bat out and looks to defend but gets the smallest of nicks of his outside edge to the keeper who dives forward and takes a lovely catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Joshua Da Silva b Jason Holder

Commentary.Commentary: OUT! TIMBER! That is a huge wicket of Alam. In space of three balls, 2 wickets for the Windies. A full ball, slanting across, just outside off. Alam gets tempted and goes for an expensive drive but ends up getting an inside edge, hitting the stumps.
Mohammad Abbas is the last man in!

OUT! CAUGHT! The fielder there was strategically placed there and Seales strikes. Hasan Ali was looking to attack and keep the scoreboard ticking, but he holes out here. Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. West Indies are doing extremely well to ensure that they bundle out Pakistan for a low score. They have removed 2 batters post the Tea break and are into the bowlers now. If they can continue to bowl with the same tempo, then they will be able to remove the last three batters as well. Pakistan will be hoping that Fawad Alam can score some quick runs and push them past the 250-run mark. Some contributions from the lower order will help him too. Hasan Ali is the new batter in.

Right then. We are back for the third session of play here. Faheem Ashraf and Fawad Alam walk out. The West Indian players spread out on the field. Roston Chase to bowl now.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

For Pakistan, the runs are not flowing and on the other hand, the wickets were tumbling down. Azhar Ali and Azam were looking good in the middle but the former departed for 17, and Azam followed him as he gave away his wicket in the very next over. He departed on 30. Rizwan and Alam stayed in the middle together but Rizwan went back for quick 23. Alam and Ashraf are battling hard in the middle and would look to up the run rate in the next session. Will they be able to do so? Join us for the third session at 3.50 pm local (8.50 pm GMT).

This session was all about the hosts. Three wickets for them after the Lunch session and with half of the Pakistani team back, they have the upper hand right now over Pakistan. Azhar Ali was the first big wicket after the Lunch session, courtesy of Jayden Seals. Babar Azam followed him as Kemar Roach got the prized wicket of him. Holder got rid of Rizwan. West Indies will look to take quick wickets in the next session and bundle the hosts out for a tame score.

Review taken for caught behind. A loud shout for caught behind but was not given. Kraigg Brathwaite goes for it. The Ultra edge shows a spike as the ball passes the blade and the on-field decision has been overturned.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Another one bites the dust and one brings two for the hosts. This is the big, big wicket of Azam. He could have really taken the game away from them, but he does not have the desired impact in this innings. On a length, around off, nipping in, Azam looks to defend this one out, but the ball seams in and beats his inside edge, to the keeper, who takes it and appeals. The umpire just shakes his head this time. There is a discussion and they take the review, in the end. Ultra Edge rolls in now and there is a SPIKE as the ball goes past the bat, to the keeper. Cheers all around as the on-field umpire reverses his decision.
Commentary.Howout: c Joshua Da Silva b Kemar Roach

NOT OUT! Umpire's call saves Azhar Ali here! Holder angles in a full ball, around middle and leg. Ali strides forward and looks to defend under his eyes but gets hit on the pads. Ball Tracker shows it to be Umpire's Call on Impact, even though the ball was crashing into the wickets. Another reprieve for Ali.

Review time! Jason Holder is convinced that this is LBW and hence, Kraigg Brathwaite goes for the review. The main question will be, was it bat first or pad? Ultra Edge shows that the ball hit the pad first. Ball Tracker shows that the Impact was Umpire's call, even though the wickets were hitting. Will remain not out, but West Indies retain their review.

Right then. We are back with all the action now. The West Indian players make their way out into the middle now, followed by Azhar Ali and Babar Azam. It will be Jason Holder to bowl now.

Update 12.45 pm local (5.45 pm GMT) - Some more good news now. The rain has flown by and the covers have been completely removed as well. The groundsmen are still trying to mop up the region near the bowler's landing and near the outfield as well. We are being told that play will resume at 1 pm local (6 pm GMT), but we are still awaiting the official word, which should be out soon enough. The timing has been confirmed. Let's hope we do not have any more delays now.

Update 12.25 pm local (5.25 pm GMT) - Good news! The rain has stopped and the atmosphere has become slightly brighter as well. The groundsmen are ensuring that the covers come off cleanly. The two umpires are having a stroll and we should have some more information soon enough. Stay tuned for further updates.

Update 12.10 pm local (5.10 pm GMT) - Unfortunately, we do not have good news to greet you with, as it is still raining at the moment. We could have just 17 overs but they were very well bowled by West Indies. They keep on showing their potential in the longest format of the game but somehow are not able to keep that going consistently. Kemar Roach bowled with fire while Jayden Seales continues to show what a great bowler he could be for the future. Looking at the conditions, one does feel that West Indies are one fast bowler light, as the likes of Alzarri Joseph could have made merry in these conditions. But this is just the opening session of a 5-day Test. Join us back at 12.10 pm local (1710 GMT) for the second session, anticipating of course, that the rain would have gone away by then.

It has been an excellent morning for the home side. They were on the mark from the word go, extracting all the juice available from the pitch and then, making use of Pakistan's inexperienced opening pair. There is nothing much to talk about in Imran Butt and Abid Ali and Pakistan were two down by the 8th over. Since then, the experience of Azhar Ali and Babar Azam has kept the hosts at bay.

11.30 am local (1630 GMT) - It is official. EARLY LUNCH HAS BEEN TAKEN. Sensible decision from the umpires, rather than waiting for the scheduled time to take the break. The forecast looks iffy throughout the Test but we can at least hope for positive news.

Cricket updates - Meanwhile, in London, India are lording the game at the moment over England. They are comfortably placed at 203/2 in 65 overs, with KL Rahul once again amongst the runs, batting on 17 short of a ton. Skipper Virat Kohli is slowly but steadily helping himself to some form. One has to say, the English bowling attack has looked toothless in the absence of Stuart Broad.

11.21 am local (1622 GMT) - There we go. This was coming. The umpires did have a chat before the previous over but decided to continue. And as if to suggest their presence, the clouds have burst open and it is raining heavily. Off go the players. The ground staff has come in full force to cover the pitch. We are no weather experts but just get the feeling that this could be a big delay. And as we debate about our expertise, on come more covers. Might as well take an early Lunch.

Right. Ready for the action to begin. The West Indian players have made their way out into the middle. Abid Ali and Imran Butt are the openers for Pakistan. Before they bowl the first ball, both the teams take the knee and show their support for the 'Black Lives Matter' movement. Kemar Roach to begin with the ball. Here he comes...

Jermaine Blackwood is in for a chat! He says that they let themselves down against South Africa and they will look to pick it up in this series and you cannot ask the bowlers to keep bowling continuously. He says that he has played 5 innings here and he has scored 3 fifties and he would look to score a century here.

PITCH REPORT - There is some moisture around and bowlers are going to get some reward on this deck in the morning session. The batters will find it hard in the morning session and will need to dig deep to show their class.

The Pakistan captain, Babar Azam says that they will try their level best to survive the new ball. Says that their preparation was not ideal but they will put in all their effort. Says that winning always gives you confidence and so they will try their level best in this series.

The West Indies skipper, Kraigg Brathwaite says that they will look to use the moisture. Shares that Shai Hope and Alzarri Joseph miss out. Says that their preparation went well and they know that it will not be easy but they are looking forward to playing some good cricket.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Abid Ali, Imran Butt, Azhar Ali, Babar Azam (C), Fawad Alam, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Faheem Ashraf, Yasir Shah, Hasan Ali, Mohammad Abbas, Shaheen Afridi.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Kraigg Brathwaite (C), Kieran Powell, Nkrumah Bonner, Kyle Mayers, Roston Chase, Jermaine Blackwood, Joshua Da Silva (WK), Jason Holder, Kemar Roach, Jayden Seales, Jomel Warrican.
TOSS - We are all in readiness for the flip of the coin. WEST INDIES have won the toss and have elected to FIELD first.

WEATHER - Some good news to start this Test. The weather right now is nice and sunny. Although, there is rain expected to pay a visit later on in the day and it is also forecasted throughout the five days. Right now though, it is looking very good.

West Indies can be termed as the underdogs against this Pakistani side. They have not been at their best in this format, as even in their last assignment against South Africa, they folded easily and lost the series 2-0. Their batting has not risen on occasions when the hosts have needed them to and there will be more focus on them in this game. Their bowling has been fairly decent, but they need to start delivering as a team, if they are to cause an upset here. Both the teams will be looking to start with a win, as this series also marks the commencement of their second cycle of the World Test Championship and a win will give them valuable points. It should be an interesting clash. Toss and team news in a bit.

Pakistan will definitely be heading into this series with more confidence as they have been really consistent in this format, in their last couple of assignments. They defeated South Africa and Zimbabwe 2-0 respectively and showed that they had a strong unit. But, playing in the Caribbean is not going to be easy. Even though West Indies have not been at their best at home for a while, it will still be a hard task to trump them. The Asians have the ammunition in the ranks, but, will they come good here? We shall find out.

Hello, folks! After a very damp start to this tour, as out of the 4 T20I games that were scheduled between West Indies and Pakistan, 3 out of them were washed out and we were only treated to one game. Now, from a white-ball, we shift to white jerseys. The 2-game Test series between these two is upon us and hopefully, the rain does not make an appearance and lets us enjoy some uninterrupted cricket, but alas, the forecast is not too great for the first Test. Regardless, let's hope that we get some quality cricket throughout the course of the next 5 days.
